steady_state.label: mean energy against capacity at move_cost 0

fires.evidence: capacity 10, move_cost 0: mean 8.9700 against the formula capacity - maintenance - damage*repair = 8.9700

silent.evidence: capacity 1e9, move_cost 0: mean 684.8109. With no cap the energy must grow past the capped steady state 8.97; if it sits at 8.97 the cap was not what pinned it.

specific.evidence: gap between move_cost 0.0 and 0.2 with capacity 1e9 is 0.834755; the prediction is 0.6400. A gap of zero would mean the cap is not the explanation.

verdict.reason: VOID: recorded before the clamp was moved to the end of the step (`core/src/organism.rs`, 2026-11-12). With the clamp after the income `move_cost` was erased, so this run measures a dynamics that no longer exists. See `docs/FINDING-the-cap-is-applied-after-the-spend.md` and `docs/FINDING-capacity-is-the-number-of-feeding-cells.md`. Kept as a record; the numbers are not usable.

limitations: One seed, one field shape, one read budget, one maintenance.
The prediction of the gap uses the move fraction measured at capacity 10, which may not be the move fraction at capacity 1e9. The comparison is therefore a direction, not a precise equality.

This shows the cap erases the move cost. It does not show which of the two jobs of `capacity` -- the energy ceiling or the income ceiling -- should be split off, nor what the capacity of the population becomes once the cap is out of the way.
